_comment: These are hard numeric limits. Claude's reasoning/thesis step may NEVER override these values. Any proposed trade that violates a rule here must be rejected before it reaches place_order, with no exceptions regardless of how strong the thesis sounds.
acc_id_note: Your Moomoo account ID — a numeric string like '281756479345015383'. Call get_accounts() to list your accounts and copy the acc_id for the account you want to trade. For linked_accounts in wash_sale_avoidance, list every Moomoo account ID you personally control.
trd_env_note: Trading environment: 'SIMULATE' (paper trading, default) or 'REAL' (live money). Must be changed manually by the human. Claude must never change this value itself, and must refuse to place REAL orders while trd_env is 'SIMULATE'. REAL accounts require OpenD to be running with trade password unlocked.
moomoo_market_note: Market prefix for stock codes — 'US' for US equities. Codes are always formatted as '<market>.<symbol>' (e.g. 'US.AAPL', 'US.MSFT') for all Moomoo API calls.
starting_capital_usd_note: Net deposits minus withdrawals, not live total_assets — excludes trading P&L so the loss-limit base doesn't drift with performance. Human updates by hand after each deposit/withdrawal.

execution.note: mode must be manually changed from 'dry_run' to 'live' by the human. Claude must never change this value itself, and must refuse to place live orders while mode is 'dry_run'. This is separate from trd_env: dry_run means Claude logs what it would do without calling place_order at all; live means Claude will call place_order in the environment specified by trd_env.

universe.watchlist_name_note: Name of a watchlist/security group you have already created in your Moomoo app. Phase A calls get_user_security_group() to find the group by this name, then get_user_security(group_name) to fetch its symbols. The watchlist is the primary universe — populate it in the Moomoo app with the stocks you want screened each day.
universe.supplementary_scan_note: Web search scan — Phase A runs a web search for notable US market movers (high relative volume, notable catalysts) to surface candidates from outside your watchlist. Up to this many are added from the search results. Additive to watchlist_max_candidates, not shared with it — the watchlist's own slots are never crowded out by scan results.

signal_thresholds._comment: A Step-1 candidate qualifies for a Phase A news search + thesis (i.e. counts as a 'notable signal') if it meets ANY ONE of these three, computed from data already pulled in Steps 1-2 (no extra API calls). This is a mechanical gate, not a judgment call. Currently-held positions are exempt and always get a thesis regardless of these thresholds.

position_sizing.min_top_up_note: A top-up only fires if the computed buy amount clears max($1.00 broker minimum, min_top_up_usd, min_top_up_pct_of_target x target_size for that candidate's conviction tier). Below that, skip without calling get_max_tradable or place_order — a top-up smaller than this doesn't move the position meaningfully. Applies to top-ups only, never to new-entry sizing.

stop_loss.note: mode is 'fixed' or 'volatility_scaled' — toggle only. 'fixed' uses the flat hard_stop_pct for every symbol. 'volatility_scaled': stop_pct per symbol = clamp(volatility_stdev_multiplier * stdev of daily close-to-close returns over volatility_lookback_trading_days, min_stop_pct, max_stop_pct), recomputed fresh from get_historical_klines each cycle; falls back to fallback_stop_pct if historicals are unavailable or the symbol has fewer than 10 daily bars. Every open position must have this stop checked on every cycle, independent of any new thesis about the stock. A good new narrative does not cancel a stop-loss.

take_profit.note: Tiered partial take-profit, not a single full-exit threshold. Every open position must have this checked on every cycle, independent of any new thesis about the stock. A good new narrative does not cancel a take-profit tier any more than it cancels a stop-loss. Each tier fires once (per holding period, i.e. since the position last closed to zero) when gain first reaches it, selling sell_fraction_of_position of the position's quantity at that moment. After all three tiers have fired, the remaining quantity is held long indefinitely; only the stop-loss still applies to it. See sell_reentry_lock for re-entry lock behavior.

conviction_trim.note: Trims a held position to its conviction-tier target once conviction has been 'low' for min_low_conviction_cycles consecutive cycles and the overage exceeds overweight_trigger_pct — see scripts/conviction_trim.py. See sell_reentry_lock for re-entry lock behavior.

sell_reentry_lock.note: Applies uniformly to every sell (stop_loss, take_profit, conviction_trim, exit_existing), not per-reason: a sell that closed at a gain vs. average cost locks re-entry for gain_close_max_trading_days trading days regardless of price; a sell that closed at a loss locks indefinitely on price alone, until price drops back below the sale price. See scripts/entry_gate.py.

wash_sale_avoidance.note: Toggle only — set enabled to false to turn this guard off entirely; no other change needed. IRS wash-sale rule applies per taxpayer across ALL accounts, not per account, so this checks linked_accounts, not just acc_id. Blocks BUYS only (new entries and top-ups) — never blocks a stop_loss/take_profit/exit_existing sell, since risk management must never bend to a tax outcome; those sells are instead logged with a wash-sale flag if one applies, for the human's own tax tracking. This cannot prevent a wash sale caused by a purchase made LATER in another linked account after an agentic-account sell — those accounts are outside this pipeline's control; only the human can avoid that side.

entry_price_gap.note: Hard ceiling on buys — a gap this large skips the buy this cycle even if the thesis still reads fine, same principle as a stop-loss. Never applies to sells. Checked in Phase B Step 7 (price-based staleness check), before the live-order gate — not part of the execution.mode gate.

entry_extension.note: Hard ceiling on buys — skips the buy this cycle if current ask_price is more than max_extension_pct above its own lookback_trading_days-day moving average, same principle as entry_price_gap. Never applies to sells.
